author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Jean Smart and Harrison Ford enter Monday’s Emmy Awards with the chance to reach distinct career milestones as the television industry gathers in Los Angeles.

Smart could become the first performer to win best comedy actress in every season of a show’s run if she earns a fifth award for Hacks. Ford, 84, is nominated for Shrinking and is seeking the first Emmy of his career despite decades of film and television work.

The Pitt is favored in the best-drama race for a second consecutive year, and its star Noah Wyle is also contending for a second straight acting award. Mariska Hargitay will host the ceremony, scheduled for 8 p.m. Eastern on NBC and Peacock. Michael J. Fox is set to receive a humanitarian honor.

The celebration arrives while Hollywood faces production cutbacks, consolidation and anxiety over artificial intelligence. Paramount Skydance’s proposed Warner Bros. Discovery deal is among the business shifts hanging over the industry. The awards will recognize the past television season even as studios, workers and audiences navigate a rapidly changing market.
dek: Smart could complete a five-season awards sweep for Hacks, while Ford is seeking the first Emmy of his career for Shrinking.
headline: Jean Smart and Harrison Ford approach Emmy milestones
